key_insight: World Tracing bridges the gap between pixel-faithful depth prediction and complete 3D shape generation. It keeps 3D geometry aligned with observed image pixels while also hallucinating the parts hidden from view.
problem_solved: Existing image-to-3D methods usually face a trade-off: depth estimators stay accurate on visible surfaces but cannot recover full objects, while generative 3D models complete shapes but often lose alignment with the input image. This paper addresses the need for both faithful alignment and geometric completeness.
method: Introduces a generative pixel-aligned geometry representation that predicts 3D points tied to each input pixel.
For each pixel, the model predicts an ordered stack of camera-space points to represent geometry along the viewing ray.
Uses this representation to extend beyond the visible surface and reconstruct occluded or unobserved geometry while preserving image alignment.
impact: This approach can improve 3D reconstruction quality for tasks that need both accuracy on what is visible and plausible completion of what is hidden. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable foundation for AR/VR, robotics, digital twins, and image-based 3D generation.
